title: Tunable Superconductivity in 1313-La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$: Suppressed under Compression and Possible $s^{\pm}$ Pairing under Tension
authors: Yang Zhang, Ling-Fang Lin, Adriana Moreo, Thomas A. Maier, Elbio Dagotto
abstract: Motivated by recent progress in the 1313-La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ nickelate thin films (Nie et al., Nature {\bf 652}, 628 (2026)), we systematically investigate the effects of both compressive and tensile strain in this system. Self-doping effects between the single-layer (SL) and trilayer (TL) blocks are observed in our studies in both cases, but are most pronounced under tensile strain. We find that superconductivity is unlikely to emerge in the 1313 film on the LSAO substrate even with further hole doping. Remarkably, within the random-phase approximation, under {\it tensile} strain, a robust $s^{\pm}$-wave pairing state emerges in the TL subsystem with sign changes between the small electron-like $σ$ pocket at the $Γ$ point and the small hole-like $γ$ pocket at the M point. These pockets are connected by a wave vector close to $(π,π)$. Our calculations also suggest that superconductivity in 1313-LNO requires an optimally sized $γ$ pocket, because an oversized $γ$ pocket suppresses pairing formation. Overall, our results predict strain-dependent electronic reconstruction in 1313-La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and provide guiding principles for engineering superconductivity under ambient pressure conditions.
summary: This theoretical study uses advanced electronic structure calculations to map out the phase diagram of superconductivity in nickelates under strain. It finds that tensile strain stabilizes a favorable $s^{\pm}$-wave pairing state, while compressive strain suppresses it. The work provides crucial guidelines for engineering high-temperature superconductivity by controlling lattice strain and doping levels.
main_problem: The study investigates how mechanical strain (compression vs. tension) affects superconductivity in 1313-La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ nickelate thin films.
main_result: Superconductivity is predicted to emerge via a robust $s^{\pm}$-wave pairing state specifically under tensile strain, while compressive strain suppresses it. The superconducting state requires an optimally sized $\gamma$ Fermi pocket.
method: The research employs Density Functional Theory (DFT) combined with the Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) applied to a tight-binding model of the nickelate layers.
model_or_system: The system is 1313-La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, modeled as an alternating Single-Layer (SL)/Trilayer (TL) heterostructure. Calculations focus on the TL subsystem, analyzing its electronic structure and superconducting pairing instability.
key_observables: Superconducting pairing strength ($\lambda$), gap structures ($g_\alpha(\mathbf{k})$), self-doping effects, and Fermi surface pocket sizes ($\sigma$ at $\Gamma$, $\gamma$ at M).
important_parameters: Strain (compressive vs. tensile), electron/hole doping level ($n$), and the size of the $\gamma$ pocket.
main_assumptions: The RPA calculation restricts pairing analysis to the TL subsystem, neglecting direct participation from the SL subsystem in the instability calculation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures and Fermi surfaces under different strain/doping conditions (LSAO vs. KTO). Gap structure plots show the predicted $s^{\pm}$-wave gap symmetry on tensile-strained films.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares results obtained from simulations on LSAO substrates (compressive strain) versus those on KTO substrates (tensile strain), analyzing how doping and strain tune the pairing mechanism towards an optimal $s^{\pm}$ state.
why_interesting: Although focused on cuprate/nickelate physics, the methodology of using RPA to predict unconventional superconductivity based on orbital nesting and external tuning parameters (strain) is highly relevant to understanding correlated electron systems in general.
